question.problem:
Consider the functions $y:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ and $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined by $$ y(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\ {x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,f(y)=[\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1}+4{y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{2}+8{y}_{2}\end{aligned}]. $$ What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]?$
${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))|}_{{x}_{0}}=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}}
$20$ {{field-3}}

current_example.problem:
Consider the functions $\mathbf y: \mathbb R^3\to \mathbb R^2$ and $\mathbf f: \mathbb R^2\to \mathbb R^2,$ defined by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14219585/assets/61c34e114232646f5c0f0406d979baf58bdb77206dd91b4a94301002f88222f2.svg)
What is 
$\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d \mathbf x} \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{y}(\mathbf x))$ evaluated at 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14219585/assets/c09d816b00c9b46167601f480e3279c4f854b1494e47da7217bc2aca8fb98351.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d \mathbf x} \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{y}(\mathbf x)) = \dfrac{\textrm d\mathbf f}{\textrm d \mathbf y} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d\mathbf y}{\textrm d \mathbf x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $\mathbf{f}$ acts on a vector $\mathbf{y} \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and outputs a vector $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{y}) \in \mathbb{R}^2.$ Thus, the total derivative of $\mathbf{f}$ with respect to $\mathbf{y}$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{y}_{1}}({y}_{1}+{y}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{y}_{2}}({y}_{1}+{y}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{y}_{1}}({y}_{1}-{y}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{y}_{2}}({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14219585/assets/3a6d355cc1a7197df5c9daa5865c504f6f1e2bba96f34e169d9431622aae4b8e.svg) we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14219585/assets/2c1616bd7d1916e1a8a8cc840bc18b0336581c8fa7d4ffba0bf711a94f092528.svg)

- The function $\mathbf{y}$ acts on a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and outputs a vector $\mathbf{y}(\mathbf{x}) \in \mathbb{R}^2.$ Thus, the total derivative of $\mathbf{y}$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ is a $2\times 3$ matrix

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{y}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{y}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{y}_{1}}{∂{x}_{3}} \\ \frac{∂{y}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{y}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{y}_{2}}{∂{x}_{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -{x}_{3} & -{x}_{2} \\ 1 & {x}_{3} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14219585/assets/4f66af267c38be2182bfd17f4c5df1e166cb5a28674d88760ac71d0392159ac1.svg) we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14219585/assets/df73c3ab59665f3152b0ed90b001fe9354121cd146288136c423762e9d22d5ac.svg)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x)){|}_{{x}_{0}} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
